I can explain the review approach, but I need the PR diff and relevant surrounding context to report actionable defects with file and line references.

For a 19-file PR, I keep an internal coverage ledger covering every changed production file, test, generated artifact, configuration file, and document. I group the changes into risk areas and trace their connections—for example, checkout input through repository serialization, or Android configuration through the affected build variant.

To prevent later files from getting a shallow pass, I track which files have only been scanned and which have had their behavior and contracts checked. I reserve a final completeness pass for unresolved paths and unreviewed changes; file order does not determine review depth. Generated output is checked against its source, tests against actual failure cases, and documentation against any compatibility claims.

I report only concrete, introduced defects, ordered by severity, with a tight changed-line range, triggering conditions, user or delivery impact, and a proportionate correction. Before reporting, I challenge each finding against guards, callers, dependency versions, and existing tests, then deduplicate shared causes.

With no diff supplied, there are no substantiated findings yet. Any eventual review will explicitly identify verification gaps rather than imply that unchecked behavior passed.
